title: The Formation of Black Holes in General Relativity
venue: arXiv:0805.3880 (v1, 26 May 2008), 594 pages; EMS Monographs in Mathematics (2009)

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'The subject of this work is the formation of black holes in pure general relativity, by the focusing of incoming gravitational waves. The theorems established in this monograph constitute the first foray into the long time dynamics of general relativity in the large, that is, when the initial data are no longer confined to a suitably small neighborhood of Minkowskian data. The theorems are general, no symmetry conditions on the initial data being imposed.' Comments: 594 pages, 5 figures.

title: Proof of linear instability of the Reissner-Nordstrom Cauchy horizon under scalar perturbations (arXiv version with journal ref)

verification.evidence: arXiv abstract (verbatim, same as published): 'We prove that generic smooth and compactly supported initial data on a Cauchy hypersurface indeed give rise to solutions with infinite nondegenerate energy near the Cauchy horizon in the interior of the black hole. In particular, the solution generically does not belong to W^{1,2}_{loc}.' Journal reference on page: Duke Math. J. 166, no. 3 (2017), 437-493; Related DOI 10.1215/00127094-3715189.

notes: Upgrades SRC-023 (INSPIRE mirror) with a directly fetched arXiv page carrying the journal reference. Independent fetch by the lead.

title: The interior of charged black holes and the problem of uniqueness in general relativity (arXiv version with journal ref)
venue: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 58, 0445-0504 (2005); arXiv:gr-qc/0307013 (v3)

verification.evidence: Abstract: 'We establish that the heuristic mass inflation scenario put forth by Israel and Poisson is mathematically correct in the context of this initial value problem. In particular, the maximal domain of development has a future boundary, over which the spacetime is extendible as a continuous metric, but along which the Hawking mass blows up identically; thus, the spacetime is inextendible as a differentiable metric. ... This shows that under Christodoulou's C^0 formulation, the strong cosmic censorship conjecture is false for this system.' Journal reference: Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 58 (2005), 0445-0504.

notes: Directly fetched arXiv page confirms the journal reference and the 'Christodoulou's C^0 formulation' attribution wording used in the ledger.
